question: Continental Shelf which is the shallowest part of the ocean has an average gradient of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**1° or even less.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Continental shelf:-**

 
 
• **It is the gently sloping underwater extension of a continent that extends from the shoreline to the edge of the continental margin. **
 
• It is the shallowest part of the ocean, with an average depth of about 200 meters (660 feet).
 
• Continental shelves are typically wide, with an average width of about 80 kilometers (50 miles).
 
• **The Continental Shelf which is the shallowest part of the ocean has an average gradient of 1° or even less.** 
 
• They are formed by the erosion of continents over millions of years.
 
• Continental shelves are important ecosystems that support a wide variety of marine life, including fish, shellfish, and coral reefs.
 
• They are also important economic resources, as they contain deposits of oil, natural gas, and minerals.
